# 🔌 MCP Servers Directory

![version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.1.0-blue) ![servers](https://img.shields.io/badge/servers-38-green) ![official](https://img.shields.io/badge/official-25-brightgreen) ![categories](https://img.shields.io/badge/categories-14-purple) [![CI](https://github.com/Amarel-Taylor-Scott/mcp-servers-directory/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Amarel-Taylor-Scott/mcp-servers-directory/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)

> A curated, machine-readable directory of **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** servers — the small programs that expose tools, resources, and prompts to MCP clients like Claude Desktop, IDEs, and agents.

MCP is an open standard for connecting LLM apps to external systems. This repo catalogs public servers with links and install commands, and ships a small CLI to search/filter/export the registry. Entries link to their upstream projects — no third-party code is vendored here.

## Quick start

```bash
pip install -e .            # or: pip install -r requirements.txt
mcp-dir list                # list all servers
mcp-dir search postgres     # search name/description/tags
mcp-dir categories          # show categories + counts
mcp-dir export --format json > servers.json
mcp-dir generate            # regenerate this README
```

## At a glance

- **38** servers across **14** categories
- **25** official / first-party servers (✅)
- 🔑 = requires an API key / auth · transports: `stdio`, `sse`, `http`

## What is MCP?

The Model Context Protocol standardizes how applications provide context to LLMs. A **client** (e.g. Claude Desktop) connects to one or more **servers**, each of which exposes *tools* (actions), *resources* (data), and *prompts*. Learn more at <https://modelcontextprotocol.io>.

## Contributing

Add or correct an entry in [`data.py`](data.py), run `python main.py generate`, and open a PR. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Listings are pointers to public projects; if you maintain a server and want it changed or removed, open an issue.
